sentences.text: Mr.Vipin Yadav, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr.Sunil Pandey, learned counsel for the respondent/State.

The prosecution case, in brief, is that on 23.11.2000 the Senior Food Inspector inspected the firm of the petitioner, namely, Ballarmal sh Khattumal situated in Mukadamganj, District Jabalpur wherein the e samples of 'Maida', 'Suji' and 'Atta' were taken.
After taking the ad sample of 600 gms. of 'Maida', it was divided into three parts.
One Pr sample was sent for Food Analysis.

The report of the Analyst received in which the food item-'Maida' was found to be misbranded and of a hy sub-standard, which is an offence under sections 2 & 7 read with section 16 of the Food Adulteration Act.
Complaint was filed on ad 19.3.2002 by the Food Inspector before the Judicial Magistrate First M Class, Jabalpur.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First M Class, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 is the manufacturer of 'Maida' which was being sold in sealed packet.

The respondent No.3 is the of nominated person on behalf of respondent No.2.
rt 2.
According to the petitioner, the trial is in progress before ou the Special Court, Jabalpur under the Municipalities Act.

The present petition has been filed under section 482 of the Code of Criminal C Procedure to invoke the extraordinary jurisdiction of this Court and for h quashing of the criminal case No.607/2002 pending before the Judicial ig Magistrate First Class, Jabalpur.

entities.text: Judicial ig Magistrate First Class, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: H 3. It is stated that the sample was taken on 23.11.2000 and the report was received on 25.1.2001.
However, charge-sheet has been filed on 19.2.2002, after a period of one year of the receiving of the report from the Analyst.
It is also contended that the petitioner has not been informed about the report of the Food Analyst.
It is mandatory under section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954 to inform the accused about the report.

It is also contended that the complaint has been filed on 19.2.2002 and is pending even after 16 years of its filing.
4. On behalf the respondent the petition is opposed vehemently and it is stated that the food items were found sub- standard and, therefore, the criminal proceeding does not call for any interference.
5. Perused the record.

The provision of section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act provides as under:-
"13.

sentences.text: (2) On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from sh whom the same of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under section 14A, e forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result ad of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such Pr person or persons that if it is so desired, either or both of them may make an application to the court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the a copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local hy (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory."
6. When the report from the Food Analyst has been received ad by the Food Inspector, it was mandatory for informing the same to the M accused persons about the result of the Food Analyst.
If the prosecution intended to proceed against the accused persons, the same of has to be complied with.

In paragraph 17 of the statement of Food rt Inspector (PW.1), he has admitted that no such intimation was given to ou the accused with regard to report of the Analyst that it was sub- standard food item.
If the petitioner wanted to examine the second C sample at the Central Laboratory, it was necessary to inform the h accused.
Because of this, the petitioner had no opportunity to exercise ig his right of sending the second sample for analysis.
The valuable right H of the petitioner has been infringed and there seems to be no justification for the delay in not providing the information to the petitioner.

The mandatory provision of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act regarding intimation about the report of the Public Analyst is to take the option in the Court regarding sending of second sample to the Central Food Laboratory have not been complied with.
It amounts to deprivation of the accused by his important right and defence.
Without notice to the accused is not expected to move to the Court for sending the other sample for Director of the Central Food Laboratory.
The sample report was received by the Food Inspector on 25.1.2001.
However, the criminal case was instituted on 19.2.2002, almost after a period of one year.
The delay in filling the complaint has not been justified.
It is also to be seen that unusual delay in launching the prosecution has resulted in denial of opportunity to the petitioner/accused of his right under section 13(2) of the Act.
This is the only method, by which, the petitioner could have effectively challenged the report of the Public Analyst.
In this regard, reliance can be placed on the decision in the case of Suresh Narayan and others vs. State of M.P. reported as 2003 (2) MPHT sh 178. e 7.

entities.text: Suresh Narayan and others vs. State of M.P. reported as 2003 (2) MPHT sh 178. e 7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When the mandatory provision of section 13(2) of the ad Food Adulteration Act has not been complied with and the important Pr right of the accused has been infringed, further proceeding in this regard would be inappropriate.

Keeping in view that the sample was a taken on 23.11.2000 and the criminal complaint case was filed on hy 19.2.2002, which is still pending for disposal even after lapse of about ad 16 years and for the reasons stated hereinabove, this petition is M allowed.
8.
The proceeding of Criminal Case No.607/2002 pending of before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Jabalpur is quashed in so far as the present petition-Harish Kumar Rijhwani is concerned.
